strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy special.hyp1f1 complex-z numerical correctness regression (SciPy PR #20805). The failing transition is a new test asserting hyp1f1(a,b,z) matches high-precision reference values (mpmath/WolframAlpha) for several complex inputs. Build SciPy under the same toolchain and MKL backend configuration described, then run the specific pytest test that checks those complex-z cases.

system_packages: Intel oneAPI compilers (for SciPy build with MKL; required to link/use MKL as described)
build_commands:
# 0) Obtain SciPy sources at the two revisions
#    - Buggy: dc9cbc03c039 (the reported buggy revision)
#    - Fixed: PR #20805 merge commit (or the revision after the fix; see risks)
#
# 1) Create venv and install build/test requirements
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pip install numpy pytest mpmath

# 2) Export MKL paths as indicated by the reproducer (adjust if your oneAPI install differs)
export MKLROOT=/opt/intel/oneapi/mkl/latest
export MKL_PKG_CONFIG_PATH=/opt/intel/oneapi/mkl/2023.2.0/lib/pkgconfig

# 3) Build SciPy using MKL (linking to mkl-dynamic-lp64-seq)
#    Use the same C/Fortran compilers as your oneAPI setup.
#    Ensure SciPy is built from source (not a wheel), because the bug is in compiled code paths.
export CC=icc
export CXX=icpc
export FC=ifort

# Optional but recommended for determinism:
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
export VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1

# Configure BLAS/LAPACK to MKL
# (Exact flags may vary by SciPy build system; the critical constraint is MKL 2023.2.)
python -m pip install -v -e . --no-build-isolation \
  --config-settings="--global-option=--mkl" || true

# If above does not work in your environment, use SciPy's recommended mkl build approach for your version.
# The key is that SciPy must link against MKL 2023.2 mkl-dynamic-lp64-seq for BLAS/LAPACK.
pinned_because: pythran 0.15.0 (explicit in the issue#20797 reproducer; included to match compiled-special-function generation behavior even though it is not the numerically relevant dependency per supplied evidence)
pybind11 2.12.0 (explicit in the issue#20797 reproducer; kept consistent with the described build dependency set)
BLAS/LAPACK backend MKL 2023.2 (explicit and numerically relevant per evidence; the defect is exercised through compiled special-function implementations)

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision dc9cbc03c039, the assertion in test_complex_z fails for at least one parameter set (e.g. for a=-0.25, b=0.5, z=1+2j, the buggy result is observed as something like (1+0j) rather than the reference). On the fixed revision (the commit after PR #20805’s fix/merge), test_complex_z passes for all non-xfail cases (with the two xfail cases remaining xfailed).
strategy.numerical_probe: The test checks: h = scipy.special.hyp1f1(a,b,z) and asserts it is close to the provided complex reference values with rtol=4e-15.
risks: Fixed revision is not explicitly identified by commit hash in the supplied evidence. You must map “PR #20805 fixed” to a specific Git revision (e.g., PR merge commit or the commit where the missing line in cchg() was restored). Without that, the PASS-on-fixed transition cannot be verified.

This defect is exercised through compiled special-function code paths that may depend on the BLAS/LAPACK backend. The strategy explicitly relies on MKL 2023.2 (mkl-dynamic-lp64-seq) as numerically relevant (per evidence). If you build without MKL 2023.2, the bug may not reproduce or may reproduce differently.

Complex branch/accuracy behavior may be input-path dependent. The transition hinges on exercising the complex-z branch affected by the cchg() change; using the exact test parameters (especially z=1+2j) is important.

Architectural/toolchain differences: only specify compilers/OS at a high level (oneAPI toolchain). On non-x86_64 or with a different compiler/MKL build, behavior may differ; ensure the same architecture and toolchain family.

The environment constraints for NumPy and SciPy are unbounded in the supplied evidence (no documented versions provided). Use the described SciPy source revision and an up-to-date NumPy compatible with building; do not assume a specific NumPy version unless you can match it from the original reproducer outside this evidence set.

oracle.reference_source: Reference values in test were computed with mpmath.hyp1f1(a,b,z) and verified with Wolfram Alpha/Matlab (and a Matlab session for the z=7-24j case).
oracle.why: The project test uses assert_allclose with rtol=4e-15 against hard-coded complex references; the bug causes obviously incorrect or very inaccurate results, exceeding this tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: test_complex_z computes h = sc.hyp1f1(-0.25, 0.5, 1+2j) (and other complex cases) and compares to the hard-coded references with rtol=4e-15. On dc9cbc03c039, the returned value is grossly wrong (e.g. (1+0j) for that input), so assert_allclose fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the revision after PR #20805’s fix (restoring the missing line in cchg()), sc.hyp1f1 returns values matching the hard-coded complex references within rtol=4e-15 for all non-xfail cases; therefore test_complex_z passes.
